title: Dub Factory
notes: Round 1: dub drums on A-D with one slow modulator each, a four-note bass on F (JC303 in round 1, Obxd since 2026-09-02), and E/G/H empty. Owner brief 2026-09-02: 'Genre Dub. 4 on the floor beat with a bit of modulation for groups 1-4 first' and 'for group F a groovy baseline, all generation off, a few notes on the bar, supporting the drums'. PROMOTED TO THE FACTORY SNAPSHOT 2026-09-06, replacing 018-generative-techno-main-insert. bootstrap.sh places this file in bank 000 and over default.zss; 018 and 017 go into the bank and never over it.

0.why: four on the floor, the anchor

4.why: E left silent this round; still carries 018's voice override

5.why: G G F C on steps 0/6/10/14 - root, root, flat seventh, fourth. TEST CONFIGURATION 2026-09-02: octave moved -1 to 0 and chord set to 3 (TRI). A triad at G1 is mud, so a chord test down there would be inconclusive; at octave 0 the figure is G2 G2 F3 C3 and every voicing is audible. Starting ON a triad rather than OFF so the feature is heard on load rather than only after a knob turn.  PROMOTED FROM TEST TO SHIPPED CONFIGURATION 2026-09-06, when 019 became the factory snapshot. It is no longer a test and there is no revert pending: this is what the owner heard at the rig on 2026-09-05 and accepted, and reverting it now would make the factory default a sound nobody has played. The wording above is kept because it is the only record of WHY the choice was made; read it as the reasoning, not as a plan to undo it.

6.why: G plays CHORDS, which the generator cannot write - see the chords block. This entry is not what sounds; it is the octave the pads colour against, and what the generator would write on steps 6 and 14 if ownership were ever handed back.

7.why: H is a deep pad: ONE chord a bar, held almost the whole bar. Like G it is authored as a take, so this entry is the octave the pads colour against and what the generator would write on step 0 if ownership were handed back.

6.why: G minor - G3 Bb3 D4 - on the and of beat 2
the flat-seventh chord voiced up, A3 C4 F4, on the and of beat 4. i to bVII is the dub progression, and this voicing keeps all three notes inside the pad keyboard

7.why: G minor voiced open and low - G2 D3 Bb3, root, fifth, tenth - one chord a bar held 15 of 16 steps, which is 1.9 s at 120 BPM. The tenth rather than a close third so it does not crowd the 303 bass, and the one-step gap before the retrigger keeps the note clear of the loop wrap.

6.name: BzSYN PolySynth
6.why: Chosen off Obxd's own amp envelope rather than by name: attack 0.0, the only instant attack among the high-voicecount candidates, which is what makes a chord audible AS a chord instead of a smear. voicecount forced to 1.0 = 8 voices because the patch ships at 0.716 and a 9TH is five notes; unison forced OFF because the patch ships at 0.483 and unison stacks voices per note, which would exhaust the polyphony a chord needs. See the engines block. PROMOTED FROM TEST TO SHIPPED CONFIGURATION 2026-09-06, when 019 became the factory snapshot. It is no longer a test and there is no revert pending: this is what the owner heard at the rig on 2026-09-05 and accepted, and reverting it now would make the factory default a sound nobody has played. The wording above is kept because it is the only record of WHY the choice was made; read it as the reasoning, not as a plan to undo it.

7.name: Analog Brass Chrds
7.why: 018 had a BASS preset on the LEAD chain at voicecount 0.25, which is TWO voices - a three-note chord would silently lose a note. 0.575 is the scale point for 5. The rest of the patch comes from the preset, because the restore writes saved controllers OVER the preset and keeping 018's 82 would have made the swap inaudible.

8.name: TapeStrings
8.why: 018 had DexKeys02 here, a KEYS patch - plucked attack, wrong for a sustained pad. TapeStrings was chosen off the patch data rather than the name: DEF1_MONO 0 so it can hold a chord, DCA1_ATTACK 0.81 the slowest swell in the bundle, DCA1_RELEASE 0.73 for the tail, and DCF1_CUTOFF 0.35 which is the darkest of the candidates. Haze01 read like the obvious pick by name and is DEF1_MONO 1 - it would have collapsed the chord to one note.

6.why: TEST CONFIGURATION, 2026-09-02. F was JC303, which is a MONOSYNTH by design - it cannot prove anything about CHORD, and F is the only channel where the verb is live (E is a sampler, G and H are takes, and CHORD draws dead on all three). Obxd is the one plugin whose voicecount scale points and bank naming are already verified here. The JC303 it replaced, with its four tuned controllers (_decay 0.35, _envmod 0.30, _resonance 0.28, _cutoff 0.50), is at git 7e013f0 if it is ever wanted back. PROMOTED FROM TEST TO SHIPPED CONFIGURATION 2026-09-06, when 019 became the factory snapshot. It is no longer a test and there is no revert pending: this is what the owner heard at the rig on 2026-09-05 and accepted, and reverting it now would make the factory default a sound nobody has played. The wording above is kept because it is the only record of WHY the choice was made; read it as the reasoning, not as a plan to undo it.

mods.why: a 16-bar breath on the kick. Depth 100 is plus or minus half the verb range, so 15 is 19 plus or minus 7.5 - about 7 dB of swing. Was 6, which is 0.26 dB and inaudible on a kick; owner asked for 15 by ear, 2026-09-02. Depth 15 -> 16 with the 2026-09-02 loudness ramp, so the swing keeps its proportion to the new base
the snare tail opens and closes
the clap echo comes and goes - the dub move
the stab's echo swells and recedes over three bars - 45 plus or minus 20
and its room opens and closes over eight, out of phase with the echo so the two never peak together

the hats breathe against everything else - 19 plus or minus 15, so they nearly vanish at the trough every four bars. Was 14; owner asked for 30 by ear, 2026-09-02. Depth 30 -> 33 with the 2026-09-02 loudness ramp; this is the modulator that sets the ceiling - base 67 plus depth 33 is exactly 100

levels_why: The owner's mix, tuned by ear at the rig 2026-09-02 and then ramped for loudness with every ratio preserved. Measured on zynmixer's main bus over 40 s: peak -7.76 dBFS before, -3.99 dBFS after, RMS -23.34 -> -20.34, zero samples within 0.1 dB of full scale. The ceiling is the HATS modulator, not the faders: base 62 + depth 30 was already 92 of 100, so everything could only go up by 100/92 = 1.087 before that sweep would clip its own range. Main took the rest, 0.774 -> 1.0. Going louder than -4 dBFS needs a gain stage on the main bus, not a fader; the owner chose to stop here 2026-09-02. NOTE for channels 0 and 3: the level named here is the modulator's BASE, not a fader reading. A modulated strip's saved fader is wherever the LFO happened to be at save time, and the builder computes the base FROM the strip - so copying a saved fader for a modulated channel sets a base the owner never chose. 0.77 and 0.67 are the bases; base+depth is 93 and 100. MAIN PULLED 1.0 -> 0.28 ON 2026-09-06, WHEN 019 BECAME THE FACTORY SNAPSHOT. The mix above is untouched - every ratio between the eight channels is the one the owner tuned - and only the output stage moved. The reason is that the two measurements of this bus disagree by 11 dB and the file did not change between them: peak -3.99 dBFS with zero samples near full scale on 2026-09-02, against peak +7.0 dBFS with 1.21 % of samples over 1.0 on 2026-09-05 (RMS -20.34 -> -10.70, crest ~17.7 dB, so it is the kick and the clap and not a hot mix). What happened in between is the wet-law fix of 2026-09-04: 019's four MODULATED sends self-correct on load, because the driver owns a modulator's base as a PERCENT and writes base+offset through _set_wet, so they came back 35-50 dB louder into a main fader still at 1.0. -11.06 dB restores the ceiling the owner actually chose rather than merely getting under zero: predicted peak -4.06 dBFS against the -3.99 of 2026-09-02. CONFIRMED ON THE RIG 2026-09-06 AND 0.28 STANDS. Read over 96 s - FORTY-EIGHT BARS, the LCM of the six modulator periods (16, 8, 6, 8, 4 and 3 bars) - with 019 loaded and playing at a known fader of 0.45: peak -0.39 dBFS, RMS -18.36, zero of 9,216,000 samples clipped, per-bar peak spread 1.59 dB. Back-computed that is a unity peak of +6.55 dBFS, agreeing with the gate's +7.0 within 0.45 dB, and it puts 0.28 at about -4.5 dBFS - half a decibel under the ceiling rather than the -4.06 the arithmetic said. DO NOT MEASURE THIS BUS OVER A SHORT WINDOW. A 10-bar read of this file at 0.28 returned -8.11 dBFS, 3.6 dB low, and that reading was used to raise the fader to 0.45 - which put the peak 0.4 dB from full scale. Reverted. Locking to a BAR is what the trap file says and it is not enough on a snapshot carrying a 16-bar modulator: lock to the longest thing that moves. CONFIRMED AT 0.28 ITSELF, 2026-09-06, and this is the reading to trust because the fader was READ BACK rather than assumed: /mixer/fader16 returned 0.2800 and all eight channel faders matched this file, with 0 and 3 visibly modulating. 96 s, forty-eight bars: peak -2.43 dBFS, RMS -20.37, crest 17.9 dB, ZERO of 9,216,000 samples at or over full scale, per-bar peak spread 1.46 dB. RMS is within 0.03 dB of the -20.34 the owner tuned by ear on 2026-09-02, so the mix arrives at the level it was built at, with 2.43 dB of peak headroom. 0.28 SHIPS AND SHOULD NOT BE MOVED AGAIN WITHOUT A 48-BAR READ AND A FADER READBACK. Loose end, recorded rather than explained: this is 2.1 dB hotter than the earlier 48-bar read at a nominal 0.45 predicts. That earlier read had no fader readback and is the suspect one.
drums_why_gate_went: Every drum carried a `gate` with a sentence beside it and NOTHING READ IT: the drum writer hardcodes a one-step duration and `gate` does not exist on a drum at all - VERB_KINDS puts it on voices only. Removed 2026-09-02, and a test now fails on any manifest key the builder does not consume. The four values were 45, 40, 40 and 25 if they are ever wanted for a feature that reads them.
reproduces_shipped_file: NO, AND THE GAP IS NAMED SO IT CANNOT BE MISTAKEN FOR DRIFT. Rebuilding from this manifest does NOT reproduce snapshot/019-dub-factory.zss: nineteen FX wet ports come out 20-45 dB louder, because the shipped .zss was written under the OLD wet law (percent mapped linearly onto -70..+10 dB) and the builder now uses tlib.wet_db, the ordinary audio taper. Everything else matches byte for byte - checked 2026-09-06 with a full structural diff, and those nineteen values were the only differences. THE SHIPPED FILE IS DELIBERATELY THE ONE THAT WAS NOT REBUILT. It is what the owner heard at the rig on 2026-09-05 and called 'fine for now', and promoting a file nobody has played would have made the factory default an untested one. A rebuild is item 50's fix - the whole pack is dry - and it belongs to item 49's preset rebuild, where the new sound gets an ear gate. Until then this manifest describes the INTENT and the .zss holds the EVIDENCE, and the difference is exactly nineteen numbers.
